decision.question: Are the scene's tonal modeling and reflections represented as pencil-drawn shading rather than retained photographic rendering?
decision.criteria: Pass if pencil-rendered tonal values broadly convey the scene's volume, lighting and reflective surfaces through stroke density, hatching, form-following graphite marks or convincing rubbed graphite tones. Smooth shading can satisfy this condition when it visibly reads as graphite rendering. Isolated imperfect surfaces do not require failure. Fail if substantial surfaces retain photographic gradients, realistic specular reflections or photographic tonal modeling underneath added grain or strokes. Pencil-like surface marks, stronger outlines and desaturation alone do not satisfy this tonal-modeling condition. Assess tonal representation independently of contour linework and the mere presence of surface marks. Use unknown only when visual evidence is insufficient to establish the tonal-rendering style.
decision.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the instruction to change the image into pencil drawing. Independently judge this tonal-rendering condition as pass, fail or unknown. Inspect the pitcher and wine glass gradients and highlights, the volume modeling of sprouts and carrots, and shaded food, plate and table surfaces. Determine whether the tonal transitions and reflections themselves broadly read as graphite-rendered values or remain photographic beneath added texture. Cite concrete regions and the visible shading characteristics supporting that distinction. Stroke-density modeling, hatching, form-following marks and convincing rubbed graphite tones can establish pencil shading; smooth transitions and preserved lighting geometry alone cannot establish retained photography, since smooth graphite rendering is allowed. Conversely, surface speckling, desaturation and contour changes alone cannot establish converted tonal modeling. Assess the breadth of pencil-rendered modeling across the scene without requiring every highlight or isolated surface to be perfect. Use unknown only when the visual evidence cannot establish tonal-rendering style, not merely because confidence is low or assessments disagree. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.
